meta.title: Percent sold is cash over post-money
meta.summary: SAMPLE pre $8M, raise $2M → post $10M, sold 20%. Listen for pre vs post.

success.message:
Session complete. Post-money = pre + cash. Percent sold ≈ cash / post. Ask pre vs post.

SAMPLE: $2M on $10M post = 20%.

start.message:
SAMPLE: pre-money $8M, raise $2M. What percent did you sell?

Which denominator?

wrong_start_pre.message:
That uses the wrong denominator. Investor % is cash/post, not cash/pre.

Return to post.

wrong_start_two.message:
Dollars are not percents. 2/10=20%.

Return to post.

listen.message:
A term sheet says '$8M' without pre or post.

What do you do?

choices.label: Ask pre vs post — it changes the sold percent

wrong_listen_assume_pre.message:
Ambiguity is the trick. The math changes if $8M is already post.

Revisit the question.

wrong_listen_assume_post.message:
Same problem. Force the word pre or post.

Revisit the question.

check.message: Pre $8M, raise $2M. If someone used pre as the base they said 25%. True sold?

wrong_check_25.message:
25 vs 20 is a real extra fifth of the company in the story. Use post.

Try the check again.

wrong_check_80.message:
Founders remaining is 80%; sold is 20%. The question was percent sold.

Try the check again.
